summary: Implemented IHasWebPages on Plugin (ADR-016 clauses 1, 2, 6, and 7 second bullet) and a secret-free embedded read/write dashboard settings page. Plugin now implements MediaBrowser.Model.Plugins.IHasWebPages and returns one PluginPageInfo (Name 'ArrTags', EnableInMainMenu = false) whose EmbeddedResourcePath is the embedded Configuration/config.html with the explicit logical name 'ArrTags.Configuration.config.html' (Plugin.SettingsPageResourceName). ArrTags.csproj embeds that file with the explicit LogicalName. The page follows the pinned in-tree Jellyfin page pattern: the configPage/pluginConfigurationPage/configPage element, data-require="emby-input,emby-button,emby-checkbox", the pageshow event, ApiClient.getPluginConfiguration/updatePluginConfiguration, and Dashboard.processPluginConfigurationUpdateResult. It reads and writes every user-adjustable setting in the current configuration model: the Sonarr and Radarr connections (Enabled, BaseUrl, ApiKey, RequestTimeoutSeconds, AllowInsecureTls), WebhookSecret, BadgeMoviePosters, BadgeEpisodePosters, EnabledLibraries (selected from ApiClient.getVirtualFolders() by library identifier), the eight renderer selectors with bounded templates, the four Renderer palette overrides, and all 21 OperationalLimits fields with their validated ranges. The three secret inputs are password fields with no embedded value; the page embeds no secret literal and only surfaces a secret value through the same administrator-gated configuration API that already returns it. Library names are inserted as text (createElement/textContent), never as HTML. ADR-016 clause 6's explicit acceptance of the anonymous static page-resource endpoint is recorded in docs/architecture.md section 6. Deliberate scope decision (not a silent one): the page covers the current configuration model only; the v1.1 badge-value allowlist (ADR-017) and verbosity (ADR-020) settings do not yet exist in the configuration model, and their own tasks (Phase 12 / Phase 10) explicitly own exposing them through the ADR-016 settings page, so no non-existent configuration field was invented. Runtime activation (task 9.3) and the post-save reconciliation trigger (task 9.4) were not implemented; limitation F2 therefore remains open and README still states a saved change is not observed until the process restarts. The elevation-gated save path used by the page is Jellyfin's existing PluginsController GET/POST {pluginId}/Configuration; no custom save route was added.

known_limitations: The two host-guarded facts (PinnedDashboardControllerServesTheArrTagsSettingsPage and PinnedDashboardControllerPageResourceIsAnonymousAndTheListIsElevationGated) were skipped in this environment: ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR is unset and no Jellyfin.Api.dll exists on this machine. Their claims were verified against the pinned v12.0 source instead, and ADR-016 clause 6 already explicitly accepts the anonymous static page-resource endpoint, which is the clause 7 second-bullet confirmation recorded in docs/architecture.md section 6. The live-host confirmation of the route/authorization behavior is owned by the v1.1 live matrix (task 14.3 per PLANS.md), not by this task. If a future pinned host renames the controller methods or changes the Authorize policy, the host-guarded facts fail only when the host directory is set.

The page covers the current configuration model only. The v1.1 badge-value allowlist (ADR-017) and per-plugin verbosity (ADR-020) settings are not yet present in PluginConfiguration/RendererConfiguration, and their own tasks (Phase 12 tasks 12.x and Phase 10 tasks 10.x, which explicitly say 'Expose it through the ADR-016 settings page') will add the fields and the page controls. No page field was invented for a non-existent configuration property; the PageFieldsCoverEveryUserAdjustableConfigurationProperty test reflects the model, so it will require the page to be extended when those properties land.

The page depends on the public-but-unstable jellyfin-web client contract (ApiClient, Dashboard, data-require, pageshow) documented as 'public but potentially unstable' in docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md 9.2/9.6. A future jellyfin-web change may require the page to be updated; no Jellyfin 12 web-client version is pinned by the server repository.

Runtime activation is not wired: Plugin.UpdateConfiguration is not overridden in this task, so a page save persists plugins/configurations/ArrTags.xml but the running process does not observe the change until restart. This is task 9.3 (and the post-save reconciliation trigger is task 9.4); limitation F2 remains open and docs/limitations.md F2 and README.md state this explicitly.

The page's save path relies on the already-proven task 9.1 settable-collection round-trip for EnabledLibraries and Renderer.Selectors; the page writes the full eight-selector collection on every save. This is behavior-preserving because RendererConfigurationResolver.ResolveDefinitions fills missing selectors from the same code-owned defaults (all enabled, '{value}') and RendererConfigurationFingerprint is computed over the resolved definitions, so absent-vs-explicit identical entries produce the same fingerprint.
